name: Question 8
problem:
| **Age, in years ($x$)** | $45$ | $39$ | $43$ | $37$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **IQ Score ($y$)** | $90$ | $82$ | $75$ | $85$ |

The table above shows the ages and corresponding IQ scores of some of Jerry's colleagues. Compute the covariance of the data sets.
worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the means:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (45+39+43+37) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 164 \\  & =41 \\ \overset{―}{y} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (90+82+75+85) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 332 \\  & =83\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(45\,-\,41)(90\,-\,83)\,+\,(39\,-\,41)(82\,-\,83)\,+\,(43\,-\,41)(75\,-\,83)\,+\,(37\,-\,41)(85\,-\,83)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(4)(7)+(-2)(-1)+(2)(-8)+(-4)(2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[28+2-16-8] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 6 \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

The (population) covariance of the data sets x={x1,x2,…,xn} and y={y1,y2,…,yn} is given by

Cov(x,y)=1n∑i=1n(xi−x―)(yi−y―),

where x―=1n∑i=1nxi and y―=1n∑i=1nyi are the means of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the means:

x―=1n∑i=1nxi=14⋅(45+39+43+37)=14⋅164=41y―=1n∑i=1nyi=14⋅(90+82+75+85)=14⋅332=83

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

Cov(x,y)=1n∑i=1n(xi−x―)(yi−y―)=14[(45−41)(90−83)+(39−41)(82−83)+(43−41)(75−83)+(37−41)(85−83)]=14[(4)(7)+(−2)(−1)+(2)(−8)+(−4)(2)]=14[28+2−16−8]=14⋅6=1.5.
